fault: The {KEY} key feels sticky, likely from dust, crumbs or dried spill inside the switch or under the keycap.
diagnosis: A sticky key is usually debris or residue in or under the switch. I'll have you unplug the board, pull the {KEY} keycap, clean around the switch with compressed air, and test it. If it still sticks, we'll swap the switch.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before opening any key.
Touch grounded metal or wear an anti-static strap before touching the board.
Hold compressed air upright and do not spray liquid onto the board.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while working on the key.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Pull the keycap
steps.instruction: Hook the keycap puller under opposite edges of the {KEY} keycap and pull straight up. Set the keycap aside.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and the bare switch with its cross-shaped stem is visible.
common_mistakes: Pulling at an angle, which stresses the stem or scratches the case.

steps.title: Clean the switch
steps.instruction: Blow compressed air around the {KEY} switch stem and into the gaps around it. Press the stem a few times while blowing.
steps.expected_visual_state: The compressed air nozzle is aimed at the bare {KEY} switch and no dust or crumbs are visible around the stem.
common_mistakes: Tilting the can so liquid propellant sprays out.
Skipping the area around the stem where debris collects.

steps.title: Test the stem
steps.instruction: Press the {KEY} switch stem down several times. Check it springs back quickly and smoothly.
steps.expected_visual_state: The stem returns to the same resting height after every press, with no sticking.
common_mistakes: Pressing at an angle instead of straight down.
Skipping the check and refitting the keycap on a still-sticky switch.

steps.title: Refit the keycap
steps.instruction: Line the {KEY} keycap up with the stem and press it straight down until fully seated.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is back on, at the same height and angle as its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Not seating it fully so it sits higher than the others.

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.instruction: Plug the USB-C cable back in. Press the {KEY} key three times and check it registers once each press.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and the {KEY} key springs back after each press.
